U.S. inflation cools off, U.S. stocks hit new highs every day—so why is BTC instead sliding toward 62.5K?

BTC sliding to 62.5K: U.S. stocks reaching new highs drains risk capital, BTC spot buying dries up, and the weekly close will determine its fate.

Honestly, this move is pretty against common sense: U.S. inflation is clearly cooling; in theory, that’s good news for all risk assets. U.S. stocks are also indeed circling near record highs, yet BTC refuses to follow at all. During the session, it even dipped toward 62.5K, and now it’s barely holding around 63,045—just one step away from the August low. One trader even warned directly: if the weekly candle doesn’t close well, there could be another round of declines next week. In plain terms, with the same money, chasing the Nasdaq is a steady ride of happiness, but buying BTC means having to stomach volatility—institutions will obviously vote with their feet.

Simply put: it’s not that the macro is the problem; BTC is temporarily outcompeted by U.S. stocks.

Market impact
- Short term: The transmission chain is crystal clear—U.S. stocks hit new highs every day → incremental funds all rush to chase stocks, with not a cent flowing into crypto → BTC spot buying dries up → if the weekly chart closes below 62.5K, leveraged longs get liquidated in a chain reaction, and the selloff reinforces itself. Right now, ETH $1,882.67 and SOL $75.49 are both lethargic; XRP $1.002 is still falling—classic “down but not up” behavior.
- Medium term: The longer BTC decouples from U.S. stocks, the less people believe the “digital gold” narrative. If ETF inflows can’t keep up, the rebound ceiling will be capped tightly—why would capital, as a risk asset, abandon the Nasdaq at new highs to catch a falling knife?

My view
In the short term, I’m bearish. BTC is currently stuck at 63K, with 62.5K—the August low—right under its feet. Once the weekly candle closes below it, the area underneath is basically a vacuum with no buyers. ETH $1,882 is also low-volume consolidation, so expecting it to set the pace isn’t realistic. There are only two variables that could flip the situation: overflow from the U.S. stock wealth effect, or ETF capital turning back on with fresh volume. There’s no denying that the dual-track design of alternating light and dark—Moonlight handling the public ledger, Phoenix covering privacy needs—is genuinely brilliant. What’s even more maddening is its fee-charging rules. If you want to operate across models, the fee-paying channel must match the source of funds exactly, with no deviation at all. That forces developers, when writing contracts, to switch environments as carefully as walking on a balance beam. One small mistake, and the whole transaction is ruined.

Now think back to that major zero-knowledge proof (PLONK) debacle OtterSec uncovered earlier. That fatal flaw capable of magically minting $60 million USD was apparently hiding for two full years inside the underlying Phoenix verification logic. If even the most core cryptographic components can have this kind of mistake, and yet we still expect everyone to painstakingly manually validate Nonce and Gas at the application layer—who can honestly guarantee security?

title: 6 Years in Crypto: The Biggest Lesson Is Not “HODL Forever” — It’s Knowing When to Take Profit
subTitle:
For the last several years, millions of people have entered the crypto market with one simple dream: invest today, hold for the future, and become financially free.
But the reality is very different.
A lot of investors have been holding their coins for years, watching the market move through multiple bull and bear cycles. Some bought at the top, some averaged down, and many are still waiting for the price to return to the level where they can finally take their money out.
That is why I believe one lesson from the last few years deserves more attention:
Making money in crypto is important — but protecting your profit is even more important.
The Early Bitcoin Investors Had a Completely Different Advantage
Look at Bitcoin’s history.
In 2014, Bitcoin was trading around hundreds of dollars, not tens of thousands. Its 2014 high was roughly $1,017, while the year ended around $320. By 2017, Bitcoin reached around $20,000. In 2021, it reached roughly $69,000, and in October 2025 Bitcoin eventually reached a new record near $126,198.
Think about what that means.
Someone who accumulated BTC during the early years had an enormous cost advantage compared with someone entering the market near a cycle high.
This doesn't mean every early Bitcoin holder is selling or that every whale is manipulating the market.
But it does mean something very important:
Crypto markets contain participants with completely different entry prices, risk levels and profit targets.
And when someone bought BTC at a few hundred or a few thousand dollars, their psychology is naturally different from someone who bought at $60K, $80K or $100K.
That difference matters.
The Problem With “I Will Just Hold Until It Goes Up”
This is where I think many retail investors make a mistake.
People often say:
“I don't need to sell. Bitcoin will eventually go higher.”
Maybe.
Bitcoin has historically produced extraordinary long-term returns. But Bitcoin has also experienced brutal drawdowns.
For example, BTC went from around $69K in 2021 into a deep bear market, eventually trading below $16K in 2022. Later, it recovered and made new highs.
So the question shouldn't simply be:
“Will BTC go higher?”
The better question is:
“If BTC goes higher, when will I take some profit?”
That is a completely different mindset.
BTC, ETH & BNB: Great Assets, But No Asset Goes Up Forever
I remain interested in major crypto assets such as $BTC , $ETH and $BNB , but being bullish on an asset doesn't mean blindly holding it at every price.
Bitcoin remains the largest cryptocurrency, with a maximum supply of 21 million coins. Its limited supply is one of the main reasons investors continue to view it as a scarce digital asset.
Ethereum has its own ecosystem and investment thesis.
BNB has strong relevance to the broader Binance ecosystem.
But there is an important distinction:
A good asset can still be a bad entry at the wrong price.
This is something investors sometimes forget during a bull market.
When prices are rising quickly, FOMO takes over.
People start thinking:
“It's going up, so I have to buy now.”
Then the market corrects.
Suddenly the same person who was extremely bullish at the top becomes extremely bearish after a 20–30% decline.
That's how many long-term investors become long-term bag holders.
My Strategy Is Simple: Don't Chase — Trade the Opportunity
Personally, I would rather focus on risk management and taking profits than trying to predict the exact top or bottom.
I don't believe every investor needs to keep 100% of their capital inside crypto all the time.
Sometimes the smartest move is simply:
Enter → manage risk → take profit → reduce exposure → wait for the next opportunity.
If a trade gives me a reasonable return, I don't need to become greedy just because the chart is still moving upward.
A 1x return on capital is already meaningful.
A 2x return is even better.
The mistake is turning a profitable trade into a losing investment because of one thought:
“Maybe it will go even higher.”
Nobody knows exactly where the top is.
The Whale Problem Is Real — But Don't Blame Everything on Whales
There is another narrative I see constantly in crypto:
“Whales are manipulating everything.”
Whales certainly have the ability to influence liquidity and short-term market movements, especially in lower-liquidity assets.
But I wouldn't use “whales” as an explanation for every market move.
The real issue is that large holders have advantages that small investors often don't:
Lower average entry prices
Larger capital reserves
Better liquidity access
Ability to wait through volatility
Multiple strategies instead of one position
Less emotional pressure to sell immediately
Retail investors need to understand this difference.
You don't have to compete with whales by becoming a whale.
You need to manage your capital better.
The Goal Should Not Be to Catch the Perfect Top
One of the biggest psychological traps in trading is trying to sell exactly at the top.
Suppose BTC moves from $60K to $80K.
You take some profit at $75K.
Then BTC goes to $90K.
You might think:
“I sold too early.”
But if BTC later falls back to $65K, that profit suddenly looks very different.
The market doesn't reward people for predicting the exact top.
It rewards people who can consistently manage risk.
That's why I prefer partial profit-taking.
For example:
Take some profit after a strong move
Move the stop-loss higher when appropriate
Keep a smaller position for further upside
Reduce exposure when market conditions become dangerous
Keep cash available for future opportunities
This approach doesn't guarantee profit.
Nothing in crypto does.
But it can prevent one of the biggest mistakes:
Giving back years of gains because you refused to take profit.
What About BTC, ETH and BNB?
For me, these remain coins worth watching because they represent three different parts of the crypto market.
BTC— The Market Leader
Bitcoin remains the benchmark for the entire crypto market.
When BTC moves aggressively, altcoins often react.
That's why I always watch BTC first before taking larger positions in altcoins.
ETH — The Major Smart-Contract Asset
Ethereum remains one of the most important networks in crypto.
But ETH is still volatile, and investors shouldn't assume that previous performance guarantees future returns.
The opportunity can be huge.
So can the downside.
BNB— A Major Exchange Ecosystem Asset
BNB is closely connected with the broader Binance ecosystem.
That makes it an important asset to monitor, but again, strong fundamentals don't eliminate market risk.
Good project ≠ guaranteed profit.
That's a rule every investor should remember.
The Biggest Lesson After Years in Crypto
After watching multiple cycles, I think the biggest lesson isn't:
“Buy and hold forever.”
And it isn't:
“Sell everything because crypto is dangerous.”
The better lesson is:
Know what you own, know your risk, and know when to take profit.
If you invest money you cannot afford to lose, every correction becomes emotionally painful.
If you use excessive leverage, a normal market move can liquidate you.
If you refuse to take profit, a winning trade can eventually become a losing position.
And if you put your entire capital into one narrative, you give the market too much control over your financial future.
My View Going Forward
I am still bullish on the long-term potential of crypto.
But being bullish doesn't mean being permanently exposed.
There will always be another setup.
There will always be another correction.
There will always be another opportunity.
So instead of trying to become rich from one perfect trade, I'd rather focus on surviving every cycle and protecting capital.
For traders, taking reasonable profits can be more important than chasing the final 10% of a move.
For investors, diversification and position sizing matter.
And for everyone:
Never invest money you cannot afford to lose.
Crypto can create extraordinary opportunities, but it can also destroy capital extremely quickly.
The people who survive multiple cycles are not necessarily the ones who predicted every pump.
They are often the ones who understood one simple rule:
Profit is only real when you protect it.

Israel’s oldest bank to list BTC trading: this time, not an ETF—buyers can trade directly in the bank app

Israel’s largest, century-old bank Leumi has partnered with Galaxy to move BTC/ETH/SOL into the bank app, giving depositors another compliant channel straight to the crypto market.

Bank Leumi, Israel’s largest and also its oldest commercial bank, announced this week that it has entered into a partnership with Galaxy Digital, a crypto company listed on Nasdaq, preparing to directly integrate Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana into its in-house banking platform. This is a first for Israel: previously, Israelis who wanted to buy crypto had to open accounts overseas or use gray-market channels, while local banks largely treated crypto like a virus and kept it out. The launch target is early 2027, subject to regulators giving the green light. The other party in the deal—Galaxy—is a publicly listed crypto firm founded by Mike Novogratz, specializing in digital-asset infrastructure for institutions.

One-sentence translation: Traditional banks no longer dodge the crypto world—they’re putting it on the counter as a financial product.

Impact on the market
- Short term: Momentum is bullish on sentiment. The transmission path is very straightforward: one-tap crypto purchases in a bank app bring in traditional depositors who have never used exchanges = incremental capital directly supporting BTC and ETH buy orders. BTC is currently up slightly by 0.46% at $63,041.96, ETH is up 0.71% at $1,883.66. In a sideways consolidation period, what the market lacks most is precisely this kind of narrative fuel. - Medium term: Even though Israel’s market is small, the precedent is significant. Once regulators approve it, conservative banks across the Middle East—and even Europe—can use it as a reference template. And because it’s not scheduled until 2027, the more than one year of “approval progress” itself will likely become a long-term trading and speculation window.

Clearly bullish. Bank-direct exposure is more aggressive than ETF penetration; ETFs still require opening a securities account. This time, depositors can access BTC simply by using the bank app they use every day. If BTC holds the $63K level, that’s the bull side’s foundation. Iran blocks the Strait of Hormuz; BTC still hovers at 63,040 — what exactly is the safe-haven crowd waiting for?

Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz forces the U.S. to back down, and global risk assets have to go through the filter process.

Negotiations between Iran and the U.S. hit a deadlock. Iran simply flips the table: it closes the Strait of Hormuz and publicly demands that the U.S. bow first. This strait is the lifeline of global energy. Roughly one-fifth of the world’s oil shipments pass through here. A blockade is like squeezing the throat of the crude oil supply chain. Once the news hit, energy markets blew up immediately—oil-price jump expectations went into overdrive, and diplomatic ties across countries tightened as well. In plain terms, this isn’t mere bluster; it’s a real move to cut off one of the world’s most important shipping routes.

In short: the focus is that (1) oil prices will rise, (2) inflation will return to the forefront, and (3) rate-cut expectations get discounted—and crypto can’t escape these linkages.

Market impact
Short term: As geopolitical tensions escalate, the first reaction is always liquidity squeeze. Institutions will first sell the most liquid assets to raise cash to meet redemptions and margin calls, and BTC/ETH—markets that trade actively on a 24-hour basis—are often hit first. At this stage, safe-haven funds are more willing to go into gold and the U.S. dollar; they have no interest in “betting” on crypto’s digital-gold narrative. Right now, BTC still wobbles around 63,040, which suggests the market hasn’t priced this in at all. This kind of sluggishness is itself a risk.

Medium term: If the blockade drags on, rising oil prices will lift inflation back up again, and the Fed rate-cut narrative gets torn up a page. Tightening liquidity expectations is the true big mountain pressing on risk assets. In crypto, medium-term valuation logic is tied to U.S. stocks—so the “good days” are worth putting a big question mark next to.

My view
Clearly bearish. BTC looks calm at the 63,040 level, but the reality is the market hasn’t reacted yet—it’s not that it’s not afraid. For the short term, watch the 63,000 psychological level closely. If it breaks, the odds are it will go find support around the 62,000 area. ETH has even worse elasticity at 1,883, so when safe-haven money flows back, it won’t be gentle on the downside. Of course there’s also the opposite scenario: if diplomacy de-escalates quickly and the blockade is lifted, the market would move the other way immediately. That’s the biggest risk point. If you’re heavily positioned, weigh it yourself—I’m not calling for any specific trade.

Iran blocks the Strait of Hormuz, yet BTC is still above $63K: why hasn’t the market priced it in yet?

Iran cuts off the world’s oil lifeline, the Strait of Hormuz. Risk assets as a whole come under pressure, and the crypto market faces a near-term downside.

Iran directly shuts the Strait of Hormuz, with the backdrop being the failure of US-Iran negotiations. Iran demands that the US make concessions first; if talks don’t go through, it will flip the table—using the blockade as leverage. What does this strait mean? Roughly one-fifth of global oil shipments pass through here. Oil tankers from Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Kuwait all have to take this route.

In simple terms: it’s taking the global energy market hostage. The script is the same as the 1970s oil crisis—just with bigger stakes. Oil prices, shipping insurance, and inflation expectations all need to be repriced.

And right now BTC is still at $63,036. Over the past 24 hours it’s even up slightly by 0.55%. ETH is at $1,883, up 0.76%. This calm isn’t what I read as immunity—it’s more like the market hasn’t reacted yet.

Impact on the market
Short term: sell off the safe-haven bids first. The logic is straightforward: strait blockade → oil prices spike → inflation expectations rise → rate-cut expectations get pushed back → liquidity exits risk assets. BTC’s correlation with the Nasdaq has never really broken; as long as US stock index futures open lower, this little bit of crypto upside won’t hold. Also, the order book is currently thin—one news-driven candlestick can punch a deep wick. XRP has already taken a stance, down 0.12% to $1.002.

Medium term: if the blockade drags on for more than a month, the rebound in inflation is basically confirmed. The Fed’s “higher for longer” narrative is restarted, directly pressuring crypto valuations. Don’t count on the old story of “buy BTC in chaos.” In recent years, every time there’s been a real conflict, BTC has fallen first; safe-haven capital goes to gold and the US dollar—crypto gets skipped.

My view
Clearly bearish. The apparent calm of BTC at $63,036 is an illusion. This level of geopolitical headline hasn’t been fully priced in yet. Swan’s CEO says BTC could bottom in October, but small-cap coins are basically hopeless—best to have them swallowed by traditional finance.

Swan CEO Klippsten weighed in, saying BTC looks like it will bottom about a year from now, roughly in October. Why? Because he thinks: when did BTC’s last peak happen? Two years ago! If that’s the case, BTC’s situation is really uncertain. He also said the small-cap coins are “basically dead,” and the only good way out is to be absorbed into traditional financial markets—stop constantly fiddling with your own little circle. This sounds like advice for everyone to give up hope and invest in something steadier.

Impact on the market
- Short term: Honestly, this news doesn’t really count as a bearish factor for BTC. After all, everyone is waiting for a bottom now. If the CEO says the bottom is in October, doesn’t that amount to admitting we’re still at a relatively high level? What about ETH? The impact is smaller, because BTC is the big brother. Once the big brother is done, the younger ones also have to tremble.
  Where is the capital flowing? I’d say, most likely, funds will continue to drain out of small-cap coins and move into “survivor” coins like BTC and ETH.
- Medium term: The industry landscape will need to be reshuffled. Whether small-cap coins get crushed by big coins or by traditional finance, or whether they can still find their own position—no one knows yet. Regulatory trend? This CEO’s remarks are essentially a backdoor call for loosening regulation—meaning regulators should act soon and “incorporate” these messy small-cap coins. In plain terms: they want regulators to help them do the math—cut the unnecessary.

My take
Honestly, if BTC really is going to bottom in October, it depends on whether it can hold the $75.47K level. If it holds, we may see a slow rebound afterward. Harvard no longer reduced its holdings of the Bitcoin ETF: its 22.9 million shares of IBIT held steady. The selling pressure has eased, but no one is adding new positions.

The 13F quarterly filing shows that in Q1, Harvard’s charitable fund slashed its Bitcoin ETF position by 43%. Back then, the market panicked for a round and people interpreted it as “a top school is running away.” But the Q2 document shows that Harvard sold not a single additional share—the position remained exactly where it was. Along with Harvard, another disclosure came from Abu Dhabi: the combined holdings of Mubadala Sovereign Fund and the Abu Dhabi Investment Council total 22.9 million shares of IBIT, also unchanged. This size places it among the notable institutional holders of IBIT.

One reminder: 13F reflects a snapshot as of June 30, and the data lags by about a month and a half. It describes what institutions “weren’t doing at the time,” not what they “are buying now.”

One-sentence translation: Top-tier institutions switched from an “exit mode” back to “hold steady,” and that’s all.

Market impact
Short term: The direct stimulus is limited, since the data is backward-looking and the market has already digested it. But it confirms one key fact—the institutional selling wave in Q1 did not carry over into Q2. The transmission path is straightforward: institutions stop selling → ETF selling pressure eases → BTC finds support in its sideways range around $63,050. However, “not selling” doesn’t mean “buying.” There is no signal of new capital entering, so don’t expect this news to pump the market.

Medium term: Sovereign funds are treating IBIT as a long-term allocation asset—up or down, they’re not chasing. That suggests long-term money hasn’t exited, which is good for market structure. What truly determines the direction is still the weekly ETF net inflow data—that’s the direct “buy” power in cash terms.

My take
Slightly neutral to steady. Put plainly: this is “bad news fully priced” rather than “good news has arrived.” With BTC at $63,050, in the short run it comes down to whether that $63,000 integer support can hold. If it holds, prices can grind on; only a break below opens the door for further downside. For ETH at $1,882.95, the trend is weaker than BTC’s—if it can’t reclaim $1,900, don’t rush to talk about a reversal. BTC deposits get emptied in 12 hours: hacker lurked in Google account for 3 months, waiting for this one transfer

Long-time BTC holders sent BTC into a major Australian exchange, but within 12 hours the hacker impersonated the account to withdraw it—security trust, a negative catalyst.

According to ChainCatcher, a user who has held BTC for many years transferred their coins to a large Australian exchange. Less than 12 hours later, all assets in the account were withdrawn.

The process is simple—and terrifying. The hacker likely compromised his Google account about 3 months earlier, taking control of both the email and the cloud-synced Google Authenticator verification codes. He didn’t move anything until the moment the BTC arrived. As soon as the coins hit the exchange, the hacker immediately initiated a withdrawal. With the email and 2FA codes correct, the exchange validated the request through its normal process, concluded the operator was the account owner, and approved it automatically. It was cleared to zero in less than half a day.

One-line translation: What you think is “two-factor verification” isn’t really just you using it anymore—it's already in the cloud, not exclusively in your control.

Impact on the market
Short term: This is a typical “security-trust” negative catalyst. It doesn’t target a specific coin—it targets the habit of “keeping coins on exchanges.” BTC at $63,052 sideways basically hasn’t moved (only -0.02% in 24h). Trading volume is weak to begin with, so this kind of news can only worsen wait-and-see sentiment. The topics of withdrawals for self-custody and self-custody will likely heat up in the short run.

Medium term: Exchange risk controls will be put on trial—if both the email and 2FA are correct, why couldn’t they detect abnormal devices or abnormal activity? In addition, the risk of the “convenience feature” of cloud-synced Google Authenticator will be recognized by more people. Demand for hardware wallets and independent authenticators will likely rise.

My take
To be honest, this isolated case doesn’t change the long-term supply-demand cycle, but I’m clearly bearish on sentiment. When BTC at $63,052 is basically stuck and buy pressure isn’t strong, the impact of negative news will be amplified. The probability of pushing down further in the short term is higher. ETH at $1,883 is also sluggish and half-dead, and it moves weakly in correlation. What to really watch out for isn’t just that this one incident was a theft—it’s that it punctures the illusion that “2FA = security.” After this, such events will only become more frequent, not fewer.

- Coin: BTC / ETH
- Direction: Negative catalyst 📉 Predicts a drop
- Duration: BTC 12 hours / ETH 24 hours

BTC deposited into exchanges and emptied within 12 hours: hacker was lurking for 3 months, and the platform even manually cleared the withdrawal

An Australian major exchange allowed a hacker to withdraw by treating them as the “account owner,” wiping out long-term users’ assets.

According to ChainCatcher, a long-term user transferred BTC to a large Australian exchange, and within less than 12 hours, all assets in the account were withdrawn. The hacker didn’t use brute-force cracking—first, they compromised the victim’s Google account, lurked for about 3 months, obtained the email and the Google Authenticator verification codes from cloud backups, then quietly waited for the funds to arrive. During the withdrawal process, the exchange verified the identity, determined that the attacker was the “account owner,” and directly approved the withdrawal.

One-sentence translation: With 2FA cloud synchronization enabled, if your Google account is compromised, the exchange’s account security is as good as compromised too.

Impact on the market
Short term: BTC is at $63,052, up only +0.02% over the past 24 hours, and while it chops sideways, this adds another bearish sentiment. The scale of this single case is limited, so it won’t directly shock the order book much, but it will genuinely dampen small retail investors’ willingness to deposit. ETH $1,883.1 is similarly calm.

Medium term: The real vulnerability lies in the “cloud-backup authenticator”—the Google account controls both the email and 2FA. Once it’s breached, everything is breached. The exchange treats “passing 2FA” as the same as “it’s the real owner,” and this risk-control logic has been proven to have a gap. Going forward, it will likely pressure the entire industry to strengthen withdrawal-device verification and address-change verification.

My take
Bearish. BTC is chopping sideways at $63,052 on reduced volume, and it originally lacked catalysts—this kind of security incident gives sidelined capital another reason not to enter. Support to watch is around $62,000; if it breaks, sentiment will weaken further. For a rebound, there needs to be a reclaim above $64,000 before there’s room to discuss. The risk is: the impact of a single case will fade quickly over time, and if no similar incidents follow within 12 hours, this bearish news will likely be digested by the market.

title: 9月加息窗口正在关闭，但BTC真正的流动性拐点还差最后一步
subTitle:
过去几天，美国宏观数据正在悄悄改变市场最重要的一笔交易：
市场开始从“美联储还会不会继续加息”，转向“高利率还能维持多久”。
先看通胀。
7月美国CPI环比仅上涨 0.1%，同比由3.5%回落至 3.4%；核心CPI环比+0.2%，同比进一步降至 2.5%。更关键的是，能源价格单月下降1.5%，汽油下降2.9%，而住房成本贡献了当月CPI涨幅的大约三分之二。
随后公布的PPI继续给鹰派降温。
7月最终需求PPI环比 0增长，低于市场预期的+0.2%；同比增速从6月的5.5%明显回落至 4.7%。剔除食品和能源后的核心PPI环比+0.2%、同比约 4.2%。
也就是说：
消费者端价格压力在下降，生产端涨价动力也在减弱。
但真正改变9月政策预期的，并不只是通胀。
7月美国非农就业意外减少 2.3万人，而市场此前预期增加8万人；5月和6月就业数据又累计下修 10.3万人，过去三个月新增就业平均只剩约2万人。
这就让美联储面对一个非常现实的问题：
通胀正在降温，就业又开始变弱，此时继续加息的收益还有多大？
7月FOMC会议上，美联储以 9比3 决定把联邦基金利率继续维持在3.50%—3.75%，Hammack、Kashkari和Logan三名官员主张加息25个基点。
一个月前，鹰派还有充分理由：
能源价格高、PCE远高于2%目标、就业尚有韧性。
但现在这套逻辑正在被数据一点点削弱。
CPI公布后，市场给9月加息的概率还有约38%；PPI公布后进一步下降至约35%；零售销售随后又意外下降0.6%，截至8月14日，市场定价的9月加息概率已经进一步降至约 31%。
从接近五五开，到只剩三成左右，一周时间，市场已经完成了一轮明显的利率重定价。
但这里有一个非常重要的区别：
“不加息” ≠ “准备降息”
这是目前最容易被市场误读的地方。
美联储真正关注的PCE通胀6月仍在 3.7% 附近，明显高于2%的长期目标；而7月PPI同比4.7%，也谈不上彻底解决通胀。
所以目前更合理的政策路径不是：
加息 → 马上降息
而是：
加息风险下降 → 延长观察期 → 等待通胀和就业进一步确认。
换句话说，美联储可能停止继续踩刹车，但脚仍然放在刹车踏板上。

对BTC来说，这才是最关键的地方
BTC目前仍在 6.3万美元附近震荡。
理论上：
加息概率下降
→ 美债实际收益率上行压力缓解
→ 美元压力减弱
→ 金融条件边际改善
→ BTC等高Beta资产估值环境改善。
所以这轮CPI、PPI和就业数据，对BTC毫无疑问属于宏观边际利好。
但我不会因此直接喊牛市。
因为BTC真正的流动性拐点，还差最后一步：
资金必须确认。
如果接下来只是美联储暂停加息，但长端美债收益率依然高企、能源价格重新反弹、ETF没有持续流入，那么BTC最多获得“估值压力减轻”，却未必立刻获得新一轮趋势性买盘。
真正值得提高风险敞口的环境应该是：
**通胀继续下降
就业温和降温而非失速
+ 9月确认不加息美元与实际利率走弱ETF资金重新持续流入BTC放量突破震荡区间。**
当这几个条件真正共振，市场交易的才不再只是：
“美联储不会继续收紧。”
而是：
“下一阶段流动性可能重新改善。”
这两句话，看起来只差一点。
对BTC来说，却可能是震荡行情和趋势行情之间的区别。
所以我的判断很明确：
9月加息窗口已经显著收窄，暂停加息正在成为基准情景；但现在谈全面降息周期仍然过早。
宏观逆风正在减弱，这是真的。
流动性牛市已经重新启动？
还需要价格和资金给最后的确认。
市场最值得关注的，已经不是美联储还会不会再踩一脚刹车。
而是——
当它真正把脚松开之后，第一批钱会流向哪里。$BTC $ETH #BTC #ETH #交易员下调2027年中前美联储加息押注

【There’s a signal on-chain that’s more honest than the price—could the market be close to the bottom?】

When I saw the FNG index drop to 34, I knew something interesting was coming.

What does that mean? The market’s sentiment has already chilled to an icy point—retail traders either cut losses or just freeze. But at the same time, ETH has stubbornly held around 1834, and it’s still up slightly over the past 24 hours. With FNG at 34 and the weekly average only at 29—this combination is one I’ve seen before. Similar structures appeared in the local bottoms of 2019 and 2021.

The market is pricing in fear, but someone on-chain doesn’t accept that price.

Still, I need to pour some cold water on this. A sentiment bottom doesn’t equal a price bottom. A sentiment bottom only means “everyone who should have sold has already sold,” and it doesn’t mean a rebound is imminent. Whether this actually runs will depend on one key variable: the speed of ETF inflows. Big players like the Dartmouth endowment fund have recently been reducing their crypto exposure, and at the institutional level, there hasn’t yet been a coordinated push.

So who would be affected by this? To put it plainly, it’s not very meaningful for retail traders to chase in right now—but those who already hold positions can stay calm and wait for the direction to be chosen. Institutions are different: what they want is liquidity and compliant on-ramps. Bank Leumi plans to launch BTC/ETH/SOL trading in 2027—that’s the kind of real-world, tangible development. Once a fiat on-ramp from big banks is truly working, capital from outside the crypto circle can finally flow in.

From a business logic standpoint, ETH’s current support isn’t “technical belief.” It’s the concrete staking logic and the ETF compliance framework. As long as these two foundations don’t collapse, the 1834 level still matters.

So my take right now is: the short-term chop won’t change the medium-term logic. If you already have positions, don’t panic and move; if you have no position, you can slowly start building a bottom position.

One last question: at this level, would you dare to build a position now—or keep waiting for even lower prices?

看到FNG指数掉到34，我就知道有意思的事情要来了。

这意味着什么？整个市场情绪已经冷到冰点，散户要么割肉要么装死。但同一时间ETH在1834附近硬生生撑住了，24小时还微微涨了一点。FNG 34，周均值才29——这种组合我见过，2019年、2021年的局部底部都出现过类似结构。

市场在用恐惧定价，但链上有人不认这个价。

不过我得泼点冷水。情绪底不等于价格底，情绪底只说明"该割的都割了"，不代表马上反弹。这东西能不能真跑起来，还要看一个关键变量：ETF的资金流入速度。达特茅斯捐赠基金那种大户最近都在减加密敞口，机构层面还没形成合力。

那谁会因此受影响？说白了，散户现在追进去意义不大，但手里有仓位的可以淡定拿着，等方向选择。机构不一样，他们要的是流动性和合规通道——Bank Leumi 2027年准备上线BTC/ETH/SOL交易，这才是真正有落地感的事。大银行的法币入口一旦跑通，圈外的钱才真正进得来。

从商业逻辑上看，ETH现在的支撑不是"技术信仰"，是实实在在的质押逻辑和ETF合规框架。只要这两个地基不塌，1834这个位置就有意义。

所以我现在的判断是：短期震荡不改中期逻辑，手里有仓位的别慌着动，没仓位的可以慢慢建底仓。

最后问一句：你现在敢不敢在这个位置建仓？还是继续等更低的点？

Tokenized stock holders increased by more than 100% month-over-month, with $23.13 billion in monthly transfers: why is the money绕开 brokers?

💡Positive: Tokenized stock holders grew to 1.31 million—more than double—while monthly transfer volume surged 179% to $23.13 billion, with real incremental funds entering via the blockchain.

CoinTelegraph’s data is laid out here: holders of tokenized stocks (a version of U.S. stocks moved on-chain for 7×24 trading) reached 1.31 million, with growth of over 100% in a single month. Meanwhile, monthly transfer volume jumped 179% to $23.13 billion; the on-chain distributed value also rose 5.9% to $238 million.

In plain terms: more and more people find that traditional U.S. stock markets only being open for a few hours a day isn’t enough, so they trade on-chain tokenized versions of popular tickers—instant execution, and they can also hold fractional shares. The three figures expanding in sync indicates this isn’t a few whales shuffling funds; the user base is genuinely growing.

One-sentence translation: the amount of money in the stock market hasn’t changed, but the door to enter has opened a new lane—and the people who walk through that door are arriving at more than double the pace each month.

Market impact
Short term: bullish. On-chain trading activity is directly boosted; the biggest beneficiaries are likely the infrastructure for issuing and trading these assets, most probably concentrated in the Ethereum and EVM ecosystem. BTC $63,070.49 and ETH $1,883.86 are both moving sideways right now. These data provide support at the sentiment and narrative level—when on-chain activity picks up, it’s a positive input for mainstream coin valuations.

Medium term: bullish, but with sharp edges. The RWA track has expanded from U.S. treasuries and gold to stocks, showing traditional financial assets are accelerating on-chain. That’s a long-term logic for settlement layers like ETH. But tokenized stocks are treading along the red lines of securities law. The more holders there are, the tighter regulators will watch. The SEC could step in to regulate the issuance side at any moment—this is the biggest uncertainty.

My take
I’m clearly biased bullish. The significance of this dataset isn’t just the month’s volume; it’s that it validates real demand for “on-chain trading of all assets.” In terms of scenarios: if BTC holds the $62K support and effectively breaks above the $65K resistance, the RWA narrative could push it to another step up. The ETH story is more direct: most tokenized stocks run on EVM chains; holding $1,850 and breaking out with volume above $1,950 opens room over the medium term. The only risk point is this: if regulation classifies it as a violation, the track could hit the emergency brake quickly—don’t treat the current growth rate as the norm.

Bitcoin BIP Editor Removed: Not a Hack, Not a Fork—Just a Rejected Proposal

💡 Dashjr was removed from the BIP editor list. It’s rare to see such a direct reversal within Bitcoin governance, and the BTC price barely moved.

Luke Dashjr is a longtime figure in the Bitcoin community. For over a decade, he has held the merged/authorizing power for BIPs (Bitcoin Improvement Proposals). Whether a number is granted or whether a proposal gets admitted, his influence is significant.

The trigger for this conflict was BIP-110—a PoW modification proposal addressing the firmware backdoor controversy. Dashjr refused to assign it a number. The community erupted, and ultimately other maintainers removed him from the editor list.

Simply put: the person guarding the gate was replaced—but the gate is still there. What’s rare is that Bitcoin’s technical processes are famously “slow,” yet internal governance has publicly turned hostile like this—something you rarely see these days.

Impact on the market
- Short term: BTC is at $63,096.59, down 0.05% over 24 hours—moving sideways as usual. ETH is at $1,885.33, up slightly by 0.09%. This governance infighting doesn’t touch funds or computing power, so its impact on price sentiment is close to zero.
- Medium term: Editing authority has been dispersed away from a single individual. The proposal process becomes more transparent, which is a positive change at the governance level. But you still need to watch BIP-110 itself—if the PoW change is genuinely pushed forward, the power structure of mining hardware vendors would be shaken. That’s when the real drama would begin.

My take
Let me be blunt: neutral. I’m not changing my view on the market because of this. BTC is trading sideways at $63,096.59; whether it rises or falls has nothing to do with Dashjr’s presence or absence. Don’t treat governance news as a trading reason. What truly matters are two lines: (1) whether BIP-110 will be resubmitted, and (2) whether the conflict between the PoW camp and the mining-hardware side escalates. Only if it escalates is it worth reassessing risk. If it doesn’t, then we keep following the existing market logic—sideways remains sideways.

美加接近达成协议避开50%关税，贸易战雷要拆了，宏观不确定性下降，利好BTC这类风险资产。

先补个背景：特朗普之前放话要对加拿大进口商品加征50%关税，覆盖汽车、乳制品这些核心品类。真落地的话，加拿大经济首当其冲，美国自己的汽车和食品价格也得跟着涨，等于给通胀火上浇油。

现在消息传来，两国接近达成协议，这50%的关税大概率能避开。说白了，贸易战还没正式开打，双方先找台阶下了。

一句话翻译：全球贸易里最大的一颗雷正在被拆掉，市场的避险情绪该降温了。

对市场的影响
短期看传导路径很直接：关税威胁=宏观不确定性=资金观望。BTC这几天在$63,100附近缩量横盘，就是在等靴子落地。雷拆了，风险偏好回升，观望资金有理由回流，ETF端的买盘也更敢出手，直接支撑BTC价格。ETH在$1,885企稳走平，同一个逻辑。

中期更关键的是通胀路径。50%关税一旦落地，进口成本飙升、通胀反弹，美联储降息基本没戏。避开关税，通胀上行风险小了一块，降息预期反而更稳，流动性环境对加密市场是结构性利好。

我的判断
我明确偏多。关税这种宏观利空被拆掉，等于清掉了压在风险资产头上的一块石头。BTC现在$63,100，短期震荡区间大概率往上抬；ETH在$1,885，这波比BTC抗跌，风险偏好一旦回来，弹性可能更大。

但有一点说清楚：接近谈成≠已经签了，中间出反复的可能性存在。这种宏观利好属于慢变量，不会像ETF资金那样立竿见影，给它时间发酵，别指望一根大阳线兑现。

Bitcoin Rare Internal Strife: BIP Veteran Editor Removed, BTC Falls Only 0.05% in 24 Hours

A long-time Bitcoin developer, Dashjr, has been removed from his BIP editorial seat. This is a personnel change within the governance layer only: it touches neither supply nor capital flows, so the effect on the price transmission is nearly zero.

Luke Dashjr is one of Bitcoin’s most seasoned developers. The BIP editors are like the keepers of the proposal repository—responsible for determining which technical proposals receive official numbering. This time, he was ousted due to a controversy over BIP-110, which counts as a rare, public clash within Bitcoin’s technical governance.

Put simply: the open-source community swapped out a reviewer, without changing the consensus rules, without touching the code, and without affecting the coins in your wallet.

Market impact
Short term: Since the transmission pathway basically didn’t exist to begin with, the comings and goings of BIP editors do not affect BTC’s supply amount, do not change capital flows, and have nothing to do with the ETF or regulation. The market already gave the answer: BTC is at $63,096.59, down 0.05% over 24 hours. ETH is $1,885.33, up slightly by 0.09%—a textbook “no impact” kind of market.

Medium term: The only thing to watch is whether governance friction becomes normalized. Bitcoin’s long-term narrative includes a saying—“slow but steady technical governance.” Frequent internal fights could erode that credibility. For now, it still looks like an isolated incident and not a trend.

My take
Neutral—wait and watch. This falls into the “know about it, that’s enough” category. It provides no directional basis. BTC can continue to grind around $63K; whether it can hold the 63,000 integer level depends on macro liquidity, not on staffing changes at the BIP editors’ office. If one day it truly escalates into the kind of route-versus-route debate seen in the old block-size expansion war, then it would be time to reassess.

title: 摩根士丹利 Q2 13F：IBIT 增至 1650 万股、Circle 持仓翻 5 倍，还新建仓了 Solana ETF
subTitle:
摩根士丹利 Q2 13F：IBIT 增至 1650 万股、Circle 持仓翻 5 倍，还新建仓了 Solana ETF

8 月 14 日，摩根士丹利向 SEC 提交的 Q2 13F 文件显示，截至 6 月 30 日它持有约 1,650 万股贝莱德 IBIT，环比增加 23%；Circle（CRCL）持股从约 146 万股增至 832 万股，翻了约 5.7 倍；同时还新建仓了灰度 Solana 质押 ETF 和富达 Solana 基金（Cointelegraph 报道，ChainCatcher 8/14 22:45 转述）。这份文件把一家美国头部投行在加密资产上的敞口结构完整摊开：现货 ETF、稳定币发行商、矿企和 Solana 都有仓位，Coinbase 却在减持名单里。

13F 的披露规则决定了这份文件的时效边界：SEC 要求管理规模超过 1 亿美元的机构在季度结束后 45 天内提交持仓，所以 6 月 30 日的仓位到 8 月 14 日才公开（SEC 规则口径）。摩根士丹利是 2024 年起首批允许财富管理客户配置比特币 ETF 的大型银行之一，它的持仓变动一直被当作机构采纳程度的观察样本（公开报道口径）。

一、比特币部分：加仓 23%，市值反而缩水 18%

摩根士丹利的 IBIT 持仓从 Q1 的约 1,340 万股增至 Q2 的约 1,650 万股，增幅 23%。但因为比特币价格在二季度下跌，该持仓市值从 6.67 亿美元降到 5.49 亿美元，缩水约 18%（ChainCatcher 转 Cointelegraph 8/14 口径）。

同一时期它还持有 257 万股 MSBT（价值约 4,330 万美元），并增持了灰度比特币 Mini Trust、Bitwise 比特币 ETF 和富达 FBTC，其中 FBTC 增幅接近 38%。股数增加、市值缩水并存，说明二季度机构加仓是在下跌过程中完成的。

加仓名单覆盖 IBIT、灰度、Bitwise、富达四家发行方，说明配置分散在多家产品之间，没有押注单一发行方，比特币现货 ETF 被当作一类资产在整体布局（分析口径）。

二、以太坊与 Solana：第一次把 SOL 放进 13F

以太坊侧：贝莱德 ETHA 持仓增加约 202% 至 460 万股，灰度以太坊质押 Mini ETF 增加约 26% 至 510 万股。

ETH 二季度整体处于下行通道，ETHA 和质押 Mini ETF 双双逆势加仓，说明这轮增持发生在价格低位区间，属于"越跌越买"的存量配置动作（分析口径，依据持仓变化与同期行情）。

Solana 侧：新建仓灰度 Solana 质押 ETF（市值约 425 万美元）和富达 Solana 基金（市值约 226 万美元）。按 13F 新增仓位判断，这是该行首次将 SOL 类产品纳入持仓（报道口径），"首次转向山寨币"的说法由此而来（baiyi 8/14 标题口径）。

两个 Solana 仓位的绝对金额不大，但方向意义明确：头部投行开始在 BTC、ETH 之外配置第三条公链敞口。

三、个股与矿企：Circle 暴涨、Coinbase 被减持

Circle（CRCL）从约 146 万股增至 832 万股，是这份 13F 里最显眼的个股变动。增持名单还包括矿企和基础设施公司：Cipher Digital、Core Scientific、Hut 8、Bitdeer。

Circle 的增持逻辑和 ETF 不同：它对应的是 USDC 这条合规稳定币赛道，投行押注的是支付与结算基础设施，而不是币价方向（分析口径）。

减持侧：Coinbase 减约 55 万股，CleanSpark 减超 310 万股，Bitfarms 约 800 万股被清仓（ChainCatcher 转 Cointelegraph 8/14 口径）。

加仓稳定币发行商和矿企、减持交易所股票的组合，可以读成"要直接敞口、不要平台依赖"的再平衡（分析口径）：现货 ETF 和矿企提供底层资产敞口，稳定币押注支付赛道，交易所股票的估值则更多绑定交易量周期。

矿企内部同样是选择题：Cipher Digital、Core Scientific、Hut 8、Bitdeer 被增持，Bitfarms 被清仓。Core Scientific 和 Hut 8 近年都把 AI 数据中心托管业务写进了商业模式，增持名单集中在"算力 + AI 叙事"这一侧（分析口径，参照 2025-2026 年矿业公司公开披露的 AI 托管合同）。

四、怎么读这份 13F

先记住 13F 的三个限制：它是季度末（6/30）快照，8/14 才披露，中间隔了 45 天，当前持仓可能已经变化；13F 只统计美国市场持仓，不覆盖全部资产；金额口径是文件披露日的市值，不等于买入成本。

13F 还有两个结构性盲区：它只披露多头美国股票持仓，期权、空头、场外衍生品和海外资产都不在其中；同一家机构的实际加密敞口，可能比文件显示的更大或更小（SEC 规则与行业通行口径）。

横向比较会有更多信息量：13F 的 45 天披露窗口在 8 月 14 日关闭，其余大型机构的文件也已陆续公开，把各家对 BTC、ETH、SOL 的取舍放在一起看，比单读一家更能判断机构资金的分布（SEC 规则口径）。

在此基础上，这季的组合有四个看点：一是 IBIT 逆势加仓，股数增长发生在币价下跌期；二是 SOL 首次入列，第三大公链开始进入大行配置池；三是 Circle 翻 5.7 倍，稳定币发行商成为投行押注的新标的；四是 Coinbase 减持与矿企增持并存，机构在交易平台和算力资产之间做了再平衡。

五、市场状态

8 月 16 日 00:03（韩国时间）快照：BTC 报 62,975.34 美元（24 小时 +0.63%），ETH 报 1,881.81 美元（+0.92%）（TokenPost 引 CoinGlass 口径）。同期公开数据还显示 BTC 现货 ETF 在 8 月中旬处于连续净流出状态（8/14-8/15 快讯口径）。

具体的资金流数字：8 月 14 日美国比特币现货 ETF 净流出约 1.311 亿美元，为连续第二日净流出，ARKB 领跑赎回（新浪财经 8/15 00:24 口径）。ETH 的近 7 日表现为 -1.68%（Kompas 引 CoinMarketCap，8/15 口径），现货 ETF 资金与价格同步偏弱。

情绪面同样偏谨慎：8 月 15 日恐慌贪婪指数 34，仍在恐惧区间（Alternative.me 数据，Foresight News 8/15 转述）；8/15 全网 24 小时爆仓约 2.72 亿美元，其中以太坊约 1.12 亿美元（币 coin 统计，BlockBeats 8/15 口径）。低位加仓的机构披露与恐惧的市场情绪，构成 8 月下半月最明显的背离。

机构披露加仓与 ETF 资金流出并存，两种信号指向不同周期：13F 反映的是二季度末的存量决策，ETF 资金流反映的是当下的边际买卖。把两者放在同一张图上，能看到机构在"价格下跌中加仓"的痕迹，但即时资金仍偏谨慎（分析口径）。

六、口径与风险说明

1. 13F 为截至 6/30 的持仓快照、8/14 披露，存在约 45 天时滞；
2. 市值变动受价格影响（IBIT 股数 +23% 但市值 -18%）；
3. "首次配置 SOL"依据 13F 新增仓位判断，不代表该行从未通过其他渠道持有；
4. 本文不构成投资建议。

小结

摩根士丹利这份 13F 的骨架是三条线：IBIT 越跌越买，ETHA 翻倍，SOL 首次入列；Circle 持仓翻 5.7 倍，矿企集体加仓；Coinbase、CleanSpark、Bitfarms 被减或清仓。大行的动作滞后 45 天，能确认的是方向：直接资产敞口在扩大，平台与高成本矿企在被筛选。你会跟踪 13F 决定仓位，还是只看价格？评论区聊聊。

RWA has been heating up again these past couple of days. When I saw “put securities on-chain,” my first reaction wasn’t excitement—it was a question: after it’s moved, who cleans up the shareholder register, holder eligibility, dividends, and regulatory checks? If you only mint a single Token, at most you just wrap the old process in a cyberpunk coat.

I used to think of Dusk as “an L1 with deeper privacy,” but after reading the whitepaper I realized the real substance isn’t hiding things—it’s splitting regulated trading into three permission layers: who can spend, who can view, and who is eligible to receive. Phoenix carries assets with an UTXO-style Note; with zero-knowledge proofs, the amount doesn’t have to be public to prove ownership and prevent double-spends. The Secret Key handles spending, while the View Key selectively grants viewing access. Like a safe: the keys are in my hand, and you don’t have to dismantle the whole house’s door just to let an auditor look.

Citadel is responsible for proving “I meet the criteria”—for example, residency or investor qualifications—without having to hand out a full set of identity documents down the street. Zedger encodes account uniqueness, position limits, redemption, dividends, and voting rights directly into the asset flow. If the conditions aren’t met, it’s not a matter of adding it later and letting someone catch errors in an Excel sheet—settlement simply can’t proceed.

So when I look at @Dusk_Foundation  now, I’m no longer hung up on the “privacy chain” label. Instead, I’m asking whether it can reduce the most annoying parts of RWA: repeated verification and reconciliation. It won’t magically wipe out exchanges, legal responsibilities, or liquidity problems—I wouldn’t dare cheer for that kind of slogan. What actually needs attention is whether real securities issuance, trading, and settlement are getting running. What $DUSK  ultimately should benefit from is business volume, not applause for three words: “zero knowledge.” #dusk  #BTC #ETH

Berkshire Hathaway’s Buffett Goes Big in Q2, Pouring $17B to Add to Google: He Once Said He’d Never Touch Tech—So Why the Turn?

The “Oracle of Omaha” sunk $17B in a single quarter to heavily increase its position in Google. Tech assets gained top-tier endorsement, and the crypto market indirectly benefits.

Berkshire Hathaway released its Q2 holdings report, and the most striking item was a massive purchase of Alphabet, Google’s parent company. The company shelled out $17B—roughly enough to match the entirety of the prior position. In other words, Buffett effectively created yet another Google holding. For decades, the old man’s persona was “I don’t touch tech stocks I don’t understand.” Apple was already an exception; this time, even Google was added as a major bet. Put simply: in the eyes of top-tier value investors, tech giants in the AI era are no longer speculative—they’ve become new cash cows.

One-sentence translation: The most old-school money has started casting its vote for the most cutting-edge assets.

Market impact
Short term: Tech-stock sentiment gets ignited first, benefiting risk assets overall. The correlation between crypto and the Nasdaq has always been there. BTC is currently trading at $63,096.62, consolidating in a narrow range—this kind of macro tailwind is exactly the fuel longs are lacking. ETH at $1,884.63 is also lying low, waiting for direction, with a high probability of moving in tandem.

Medium term: The signal value of this move outweighs the sheer amount. What Buffett is endorsing is the entire pricing logic of AI assets; market risk appetite is likely to rise systematically. Once the valuations of tech giants are confirmed, when overflow capital searches for more elastic opportunities, crypto often ends up on the options list. This isn’t a direct positive catalyst, but it’s the type that adds bricks to the foundation of a bull market.

My take
Honestly, I’m on the optimistic side—but I need to be clear: this is a slow-moving factor, not a catalyst that will ferment today and pump tomorrow. The chain is flowing: Buffett recognizes tech assets → risk appetite rebounds → funds spill over into crypto. BTC around $63,096 is grinding on lower volume. Upward, first we need to see whether it can tag $64K. Downside support is around $62K in the near term. The only thing to watch is a U.S. stock “gap up then fade.” If that happens, BTC will likely keep bleeding higher after all.

Direction: I’m on the long side.

I watched the charts so long last night my eyes felt sore. I didn’t go guessing the next K-line after $DUSK ; instead, I drew the Zedger process in the Whitepaper’s Section 7.3 three times using CREATE, SEND, ACCEPT, and SETTLE. Only after finishing did I realize that calling Dusk just an “privacy chain” is indeed too narrow—it's like understanding a bank as an insurance safe that can count money.

Lately, RWA has been talking about “moving stocks onto the chain,” but the hard part of securities isn’t simply minting a token. The hard part is whether the buyer is on the whitelist; who owns the assets before payment is received; whether the position can cross certain limits; and who has voting rights and dividend rights on the snapshot date. A typical UTXO model isn’t great at tracking these continuous states. But fully transparent accounts would lay institutional positions out on the table.

Zedger’s solution is pretty solid: it extends the account model to record state; Phoenix-style UTXO handles transfers; then it combines a Sparse Merkle Tree and a Segment Tree into an SMST. Transaction balance, voting balance, dividend balance, and interval maximum balance are tracked separately. What’s publicly visible on-chain is only the root after a Poseidon hash. Transfers aren’t just “done instantly.” The recipient must ACCEPT within a deadline, and the sender then SETTLE; until confirmed, the assets are still recorded in the sender’s balance. That detail isn’t flashy, but it’s exactly where securities settlement disputes are most likely.

So now when I look at @Dusk_Foundation , I’m not obsessing over whether it can hide transactions—I’m watching whether it can automatically execute the rules without exposing your position’s underwear. I understand the logic, but for self-preservation, a protocol design is only the first gate; what’s really valuable will come from the issuer, investors, and secondary liquidity all showing up together. #dusk  #BTC #ETH

💡 Bearish. Israel’s airstrike on Lebanon left 11 dead; the ceasefire is basically little more than paper-thin now, putting short-term sentiment for BTC and other risk assets under pressure.

Israel launched an airstrike on Lebanon, causing 11 deaths—yet it had only been just over two months since the Israel–Lebanon ceasefire took effect. This ceasefire agreement was always barely holding together. Reports about both sides accusing each other of breaking the terms never really stopped. This airstrike, in effect, marks the harshest breach of the ceasefire so far—an all-out pull-the-mask-off escalation.

Diplomatically, talks for lasting peace look unlikely in the short term. Instead, the risk of further escalation has moved to the forefront.

One-sentence translation: The market thought the Middle East fire was out, but turns out it’s just been smoldering under pressure—geopolitical risk premium is back.

On the charts, BTC is at $63,096.62, down 0.09% in 24h. ETH is at $1,884.83, up slightly 0.03%. Honestly, with news this explosive, both coins barely moved—this is a signal. Bad news isn’t driving volume, suggesting limited market absorption power and a weak bias in the trend.

Impact on the market
- Short term: Escalation in the geopolitical conflict equals a risk-avoidance mode. Don’t count on the “digital gold” script. In the past few years, BTC has been hit alongside US stocks under similar conditions far more often than it surged on its own. Risk-averse capital will most likely flow into gold and the US dollar. What crypto investors fear isn’t the news itself—it’s liquidations triggered in the broader move. The more crowded leveraged longs are, the harsher the clears.
- Medium term: If the ceasefire fully collapses, the market will start pricing ongoing geopolitical risk continuously, and overall risk appetite will be pressured by another layer. For crypto, that means external liquidity is a headwind—ETF flows and on-exchange sentiment won’t be able to stand apart. Only a rapid cool-down can let this bearish news digest itself.

My view
In the short term, I’m bearish. The message, taken purely by impact, isn’t the most devastating—but the timing is bad. BTC around $63,096.62 has already been drifting lower on reduced volume. Adding a geopolitical negative catalyst increases the likelihood of breaking below the $63,000 psychological level. Once it breaks, it can easily trigger cascading deleveraging. ETH is weaker: $1,884.83 is still some distance from $1,900, and the rebound strength is likely to be weak. My take: heavy resistance lies above BTC over the next 12 hours—watch closely whether the $63,000 integer level can hold. If the situation in Lebanon keeps escalating, downside room will open up again. Only if both sides quickly exercise restraint will there be a window for sentiment to repair. The risks are also clear: geopolitics can come fast and leave fast. A single late-night headline like “Both sides agree to restrain” could flip the situation. The price never gave me a clear answer, so I just opened two wallet pages and mapped a securities asset from SEND to ACCEPT by cross-checking the whitepaper. At first I thought the line “funds won’t arrive unless the recipient actively clicks confirm” was a system bug, and I almost refreshed the page. After reading Zedger, I realized it isn’t lag—it’s @Dusk_Foundation  deliberately adding a gate to financial settlement.

With a normal Token transfer, it’s basically over. Zedger is different: the recipient must actively ACCEPT. Until confirmation, the amount is still counted in the sender’s balance. If nobody accepts it before it expires, it can be recovered via CLAIM.

It trades a bit of that “instant-arrival” satisfaction for something more important: securities can’t be forcibly pushed through or mis-transferred, and the books won’t be messed with until ownership is confirmed—no accidental ledger edits.

What I kept going back to were the Sparse Merkle-Segment Trie structures. Balance changes leave segmented traces—transaction balances, voting balances, and dividend-eligibility balances are tracked separately. On-chain, only Poseidon hashes are revealed; it doesn’t spill my full holdings to random passersby. When an audit is needed, the authorized party can rebuild the capital structure from historical snapshots. Spectators can’t see my cards, and the audit doesn’t have to rely on screenshots and detective work.

Recently, the official website updated NPEX’s confirmed issuance size to above €200 million. That’s more worth watching than just vague “RWA narrative.” But I won’t get carried away just because the whitepaper is detailed. The real test is whether, after the actual issuance, ACCEPT/SETTLE work smoothly, whether permissions can be abused, and whether historical share registries can be stably reconstructed.

So now I’m looking at $DUSK —not whether the privacy track is hot, but whether it can make both “confidentiality” and “accountability” into financial infrastructure at the same time. I stared at the market board for half an hour last night, but I still didn’t chase it. I turned around and reread Chapter 3 of the Dusk whitepaper. Pretty ridiculous—while others study candlestick charts, I was studying how to save myself when, at midnight, a chain “fails to deliver.” In January, when doing the creator tasks, I was watching the hype; but what truly struck me this time was this: it didn’t pretend that every node stays online forever.

Dusk’s Succinct Attestation isn’t about having all nodes crowd together to shout “approved.” Each round first uses deterministic random sampling to select a block producer from the stakers, then separately samples a validation committee and an approval committee: the former checks candidate blocks, and the latter reviews the voting results. The committees use BLS aggregated signatures, compressing multiple votes into a verifiable attestation. In plain terms: whoever proposes, whoever checks the goods, and whoever stamps it—all must leave behind cryptographic receipts.

What I care about most is its least flattering side: after 16 consecutive iteration failures, the protocol enters emergency mode, disables timeouts, and keeps multiple ongoing iterations waiting for the statutory number of votes. If network latency creates forks in the same round, the fallback prioritizes blocks with the lower iteration number, and then rolling finality gradually pushes blocks from “accepted” to “final” based on subsequent proofs.

But I won’t just pick the parts that sound nice. In extreme cases, even emergency empty blocks still include Dusk signatures—this trust boundary is worth continuing to watch. Having lots of nodes doesn’t automatically mean decentralization graduation; whether stake concentration, uptime rates, and whether penalties can truly be enforced—those are the hard metrics.

$DUSK  here isn’t only a trading code. It simultaneously carries staking, fee, block production, and voting incentive roles. From a “survive first” perspective, I won’t go all-in just because the mechanism is detailed. The real technical depth of a financial chain isn’t how fast it runs in a tailwind; it’s whether, when things break at midnight, you can still balance the books correctly. @Dusk_Foundation #dusk  #ETH #BTC

Today I walked into the office building. The security guard glanced at the access control and let me in. After I sat down, I suddenly realized that compliance should really work this way: proving that “I’m authorized to enter” doesn’t mean I have to lay out my ID card, payroll card, and exactly what time I got home last night all at once. In the past, when I looked at @Dusk_Foundation , I always felt that “serving privacy while also serving oversight” was like a resume where it argues with itself.

Later, after I chewed through the transaction section of the 2024 white paper, I found that Dusk isn’t handing privacy a single all-purpose master key for oversight. Instead, it splits public and hidden into two separate tracks. Moonlight uses a public account model—balances and transfers are verifiable. Phoenix turns funds into encrypted notes. On-chain, you don’t need to know exactly which note you spent; you only check whether the nullifier has appeared before, preventing double-spending. Amount conservation, sufficient balance, and ownership are verified by zero-knowledge proofs. Pair that with one-time note public keys that break the linkage between before and after, and the books can be reconciled without having to stand in the public square and bare your financial life.

Where it gets especially interesting for RWA is Citadel. Users can prove they hold valid credentials issued by a trusted institution—for example, regional status or investor eligibility—without putting their full identity information on-chain. When an audit is needed, they can hand over the necessary information via a viewing key or targeted disclosure. At least from the protocol’s logic, it isn’t “nobody can see anything,” and it isn’t “an admin presses a button and the whole network goes bare.” It’s about proving only the parts that need to be proven.

But I won’t clap on the spot just because it says “zero-knowledge.” Which party issues the credentials, which attributes the service accepts, how revocation works, and how viewing keys are stored—those are still governance questions. Cryptography can prove that the materials weren’t fabricated. It can’t guarantee that the person looking at the materials will never act carelessly.

So for $DUSK , I’ll keep observing. Its biggest selling point isn’t absolute anonymity—it’s enabling businesses to switch between public, hidden, and necessary disclosure. This direction is more likely than a pure privacy coin to enter real-world finance. The trade-off isn’t that trust disappears; it’s that trust is broken down into smaller, more specific pieces. Protect your principal, DYOR, and this is not investment advice. Are you more willing to accept complete transparency, or only disclose what’s necessary?#dusk  #BTC #ETH

后来把2024白皮书的交易部分啃完，我发现Dusk不是给隐私装一把监管总钥匙，而是把公开和隐藏拆成两条轨道。Moonlight采用公开账户模型，余额与转账可查；Phoenix则把资金做成加密note。链上不必知道你具体花了哪张note，只检查nullifier是否出现过，防止双花；金额守恒、余额充足和所有权则交给零知识证明验证。再配合一次性note公钥切断前后关联，账能算明白，人不用站在广场上报家底。

它对RWA更有意思的地方是Citadel。用户可以证明自己持有受信机构签发的有效凭证，比如地区或投资者资格，却不必把完整身份资料写上链。需要审计时，再通过viewing key或定向披露交出必要信息。至少从协议逻辑看，这不是“谁都看不见”，也不是“管理员一按按钮全网裸奔”，而是尽量只证明该证明的部分。

但我也不会看见“零知识”就闭眼鼓掌。凭证签发方由谁认可、服务方接受哪些属性、撤销机制和viewing key怎么保管，仍然是治理问题。密码学能证明材料没乱编，证明不了看材料的人永远不乱来。

所以对 $DUSK ，我会继续观察。它最大的卖点不是绝对匿名，而是让业务在公开、隐藏和必要披露之间切换。这个方向比纯隐私币更容易走进现实金融，代价是信任没有消失，只是被拆得更细。保住本金，DYOR，不构成投资建议。你更能接受完全透明，还是只披露必要信息？#dusk  #BTC #ETH

The sovereign fund holds up through the mark-to-market loss and “dead-grips” IBIT. The ETF-side selling pressure fails to materialize, turning directly into a tailwind for BTC.

Latest 13F filings revealed the exposure: two sovereign institutions—Mubadala and the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority. In Q2, their IBIT (BlackRock spot Bitcoin ETF) positions had an unrealized loss of about $118 million, but net selling was zero. By the end of June, roughly $764 million was still sitting in the position.

One-sentence translation: Real national-level long-term money treats quarterly pullbacks as noise.

Market impact
The short-term transmission chain is straightforward: sovereign funds don’t cut the position → IBIT’s net sell pressure disappears → BTC gets absorbed at around $63,103. The market has been worried that institutions would use a dip to exit. This data directly wipes out half of that concern.

For the medium term, sovereign wealth funds are “the longest money” in the market. If they hold and don’t leave, it’s essentially a benchmark for pensions and family offices. 从1872起步的这轮反弹，在1924.97被一巴掌拍回来。那根4小时K线成交量125万根，金额23.8亿刀。整个30根K线里最大的一根。然后就是连续下跌，连收7根阴线，从1891一路滑到1882。中间几乎没像样的反弹。

看量。反弹那波从1872到1924，量能逐根放大，有人在做多。但打到1924以上，卖盘倾巢而出。那根长上影线说明了一切——上方有巨量挂单等着接货，不是散户挂的。反弹结束。之后成交量从125万根快速萎缩到11万根，资金撤退得很干脆。

情绪面更直观。资金费率正0.0045%，低得可怜。多头不愿加杠杆，说明没人信能突破。标记价1882.09，指数价1883.03，两者几乎重合。合约市场多空都没发力。24小时振幅只有11刀，高低都在1874到1886之间。这不是蓄势，是没方向。

大户动向看两个信号。一个是1862那个低点——砸到那儿的时候出了102万根K线，金额19亿，明显有大资金在底部接货。另一个是1924那根天量上影，同样19亿的金额，有人在顶部出货。一买一卖，机构在做区间，不做趋势。

量价结构上，1862-1863是近期支撑区，两次探底都没破。1896-1897是压力区，三次测试都上不去。现在价格卡在区间中下部。24小时成交额12.5亿刀，量在萎缩。缩量区间整理，变盘在即。方向取决于谁先动手。

K线细节上，最近6根4小时K线全部窄幅震荡，实体不超过3刀。上下影都很短，说明多空都没意愿推。最后三根更是缩量到极致——从13万根、7.9万根到最新的7500根。这不是正常交易状态，是暴风雨前的安静。

妮妮的计划：

空仓。当前价 1882，正好卡在区间中间。上不突破1897不做多，下不破1863不做空。等方向出来再动。止损放在区间外5刀。

Tokenizing Nvidia’s market cap jumps another $18 million: who’s buying on-chain US stocks?

On-chain Nvidia stock rNVDA’s market cap rose by $18 million, and for the time being it doesn’t really affect the overall BTC and ETH market.

The reality: it’s a project that tokenizes stocks. Simply put, it “moves” Nvidia stock onto the Arbitrum chain and turns it into an rNVDA token. If you don’t have a US stock account—or if US stocks aren’t even open yet—you can trade “Nvidia” 7×24 anytime. This time, rNVDA’s market cap increased by $18 million, which suggests real money is indeed flowing in. The broader backdrop is the RWA (tokenizing real-world assets) track, which has been heating up. Stocks, treasury bonds, and funds are all being moved onto-chain, and DeFi wants to steal business from traditional finance using this approach. But honestly, compared with Nvidia’s sheer scale, $18 million is like picking a drop of water from the ocean. At this stage, it feels more like narrative validation, still far from any true flood of capital.

Impact on the market

- Short term: This kind of news basically can’t move the whole market. The data is in front of us: BTC is currently $63,078.62, changing only 0.21% over the last 24 hours; ETH is $1,883.5, up 0.17%. It’s still going sideways. Money is mainly rotating within DeFi’s small circle. What’s actually getting attention is sentiment among funds tied to the Arbitrum ecosystem and the RWA theme.
- Medium term: What’s worth watching is regulation. Tokenized stocks have long been stuck in a legal gray area under securities law. If the SEC doesn’t give a clear green light, this space could be shut down at any moment. But if a compliant pathway opens, and traditional capital borrows the on-chain route to buy US stocks, while crypto capital turns around to buy US stocks as well, then the scale won’t be limited to the tens-of-millions level.

My take

My stance is to wait and watch. I don’t think this news can unlock a market rally. The reason is straightforward: an incremental $18 million is just a drop compared with BTC’s day-to-day trading volume. Expecting it to pump the market is unrealistic. In the short term, BTC will most likely continue to range around the $63,078.62 level, with no catalysts driving it meaningfully either up or down. The real thing to pay attention to is the point where RWA shifts from a “small experiment” into a “major channel.” The day tokenized stocks reach the one-billion-dollar scale—that would be an event on the level of a real market move. Until then, treat it as industry progress, not as a reason for a pump.

链上英伟达股票rNVDA市值涨了1800万美元，对BTC、ETH大盘暂时没啥影响。

Reality是个做代币化股票的项目，简单说：把英伟达股票搬到Arbitrum链上变成rNVDA代币，你没有美股账户、不等美股开盘，7×24随时能交易“英伟达”。这次rNVDA市值增加了1800万美元，说明确实有真金白银在往里走。背后的大背景是RWA（现实资产上链）这条赛道一直在升温，股票、国债、基金都在往链上搬，DeFi想用这套方式从传统金融嘴里抢生意。但说实话，1800万美元对比英伟达本体的体量就是九牛一毛，现阶段更像叙事验证，离资金洪流还远。

对市场的影响

- 短期：这种消息基本带不动大盘。数据摆在这：BTC现在$63,078.62，24小时只动0.21%；ETH $1,883.5，涨0.17%。该横盘还横盘，钱主要在DeFi小圈子里转，真正受刺激的是Arbitrum生态和RWA概念的资金情绪。
- 中期：值得盯的是监管。代币化股票一直卡在证券法的灰色地带，SEC不松口，这赛道随时可能被摁住。但如果合规通道打开，传统资金借链上进美股、币圈资金反过来买美股，那规模就不是千万级的事了。

我的判断

我的态度是观望，不认为这消息能撬动行情。理由很直白：1800万美元的增量对BTC的日常成交量来说是零头，指望它拉盘不现实。BTC短期大概率还是在$63,078.62这个位置附近震荡，上下都缺催化剂。真正该留意的是RWA从“小实验”变成“大通道”的那个节点，哪天代币化股票规模冲到十亿美元级别，那才是行情级别的事件。在那之前，把它当行业进展看，别当拉盘理由。

AI creates new billionaires and millionaire-rich people; money first goes into luxury watches and mansions: has the wealth effect not reached the crypto market yet?

In the past couple of years, AI has created a batch of new rich. The money has gone straight into consumers’ pockets for luxury goods, and the crypto market has not gotten a share of the “soup” for now.

Over the past two years, the US stock market’s AI sector has been a cash-printing machine: the founders and early employees behind chips, computing power, and large models—whose equity has directly turned into billion-dollar fortunes. After these new elites get rich, their first move is not to buy BTC, but to buy watches, cars, and mansions—luxury consumption is being directly ignited.

In plain terms: wealth is indeed being created, but at the moment it is still stuck at the “consumption-for-enjoyment” phase, not yet broadly shifting into investment-type assets.

The relationship with crypto needs to be viewed from a detour: historically, in every US stock market boom that creates new millionaires, eventually some of that money overflows into the crypto market. This happened when the internet’s new rich emerged in 2000, and it happened again in 2021 when liquidity flooded into tech stocks. The issue now is that this overflow has not shown up yet.

Market impact
- Short term: The market has already answered—BTC $63,078, up 0.22% in 24 hours; ETH $1,883, up 0.20%. It’s as flat as it can get. With AI wealth-news everywhere, crypto prices don’t budge at all, which suggests this money has not yet anything to do with crypto. Funds are flowing to luxury goods and high-end real estate, not into digital assets.
- Medium term: There are two paths. One is that the wealth effect continues to build momentum: once the new rich have spent enough, they start allocating to alternative assets, and BTC as a “digital gold” is a natural option. The other is that the AI bubble narrative heats up: once AI stocks pull back, crypto as a high-beta risk asset may get hit first. Since neither path has played out yet, this can only be considered a neutral variable.

One-sentence translation: The money was made, but it’s still in the watch-buying stage—not the coin-buying stage.

My take
Neutral—wait and watch. In this kind of macro-wealth story, the short term doesn’t have a direct impact on the market. BTC is grinding in a tight range near $63,078, and ETH $1,883 is the same with no clear direction. The signal that truly matters isn’t what the rich are buying, but concrete funding data—such as the total supply of stablecoins and net inflows into exchanges. Only when those indicators turn positive does the “wealth overflow” count as truly taking shape. With news like this, it’s fine to treat it as background color; using it as a catalyst is just self-deception.

Now the玩法 has changed: 15 DeFi apps already hold $111 million worth of tokenized stocks. What does depositing into DeFi mean? In plain terms: putting stocks on-chain is only the first step; once those stocks are absorbed and used within DeFi, that’s when they truly get integrated into the on-chain financial system. Regulation still sits in a gray area, but the money has already voted with its feet.

NVIDIA has nearly $30 billion in off-balance-sheet liabilities hidden behind the scenes: an AI money-printing machine—why is it being questioned by insiders?

NVIDIA’s nearly $30 billion off-balance-sheet liabilities are being targeted; credit for the AI leader is questioned → tech stocks’ risk appetite contracts → BTC comes under pressure together with the Nasdaq.

In recent years, NVIDIA has signed a large number of procurement commitments with suppliers such as TSMC and Hynix in order to lock in production capacity—chips, HBM memory, advanced packaging—everything is placed on preorder in advance. Most of these commitments do not appear on the balance sheet; they’re tucked into the notes to the financial reports, and together they add up to nearly $30 billion. Put simply: “I’m taking all the goods; I’ll pay later.” In the past, nobody cared much because the demand for GPUs far exceeded supply—you could sell whatever you produced. But now investors are doing a different calculation—what if AI demand cools off? Then these commitments can turn from a weapon used to secure capacity into an unshakable burden; impairment gets written down—write-downs happen, losses happen.

Crypto Briefing directly compares this to a funding trap that tech companies fell into in the past. Historically, more than one tech giant has died from off-balance-sheet commitments.

One-sentence translation: NVIDIA locked in production capacity with “pay later.” When demand is there, it’s a moat; when demand disappears, it becomes a $3 billion hole.

Impact on the market
- Short term: It directly hits AI-sector sentiment. NVIDIA is the overall leader of this leg of the rally; its footnote disclosures are being examined under a magnifying glass, so tech stocks’ risk appetite first cools off. The transmission to the crypto market is very straightforward: institutional funds are paired with U.S. stocks and crypto; when tech stocks flinch, risk assets are generally reduced, and BTC’s buy-side also turns more cautious. BTC is currently hovering at $63,108—it's already waiting for a direction. This kind of news adds extra weight to the balance scale.
- Mid term: If more AI companies are later exposed to similar off-balance-sheet commitments, the market will reprice the entire AI supply chain; selling pressure won’t be a one- or two-day affair. And BTC’s correlation with the Nasdaq has always been there. During the adjustment cycle in U.S. stocks, it will be hard for the crypto market to stay out of trouble. For something like ETH $1,883, wobbling near the lows, the upside/downside elasticity would be even greater.

My view
Honestly, I’m bearish in the short term. The nearly $30 billion off-balance-sheet commitments themselves aren’t fatal. What’s fatal is that they puncture the narrative of “infinite AI demand.” The market fears most is uncertainty getting loosened. BTC at the $63,100 level has been grinding already; if the Nasdaq truly pulls back because of this, the $63,000 psychological level will likely be tested. If it can’t hold below that, it opens the door for further downside. ETH is weaker—$1,883 is already at low levels, and downside linkage would just make the drop harsher. If you want to go long, at least wait for NVIDIA’s official response and for this “mine” to be digested to a large extent. Going in now to gamble on a rebound isn’t a great deal in terms of risk-reward.

英伟达账外藏着近300亿美元负债：AI印钞机，为什么被自己人质疑？

英伟达近300亿美元表外负债被盯上，AI龙头信用遭质疑→科技股风险偏好收缩→BTC跟着纳指一起承压。

英伟达这些年为了锁产能，跟台积电、海力士这类供应商签了大量采购承诺——芯片、HBM内存、先进封装，全要提前下订。这些承诺大部分不进资产负债表，藏在财报附注里，加起来逼近300亿美元。说白了：货我全要了，钱以后付。以前没人当回事，因为GPU供不应求，砸多少卖多少。但现在投资者开始算另一笔账——万一AI需求降温，这些承诺就从抢产能的武器变成甩不掉的包袱，该减值减值，该亏亏。Crypto Briefing直接把这个类比为当年科技公司栽过的融资陷阱，历史上死在表外承诺上的科技巨头不是一家两家。

一句话翻译：英伟达用“以后付钱”锁死了产能，需求在就是护城河，需求没了就是300亿的坑。

对市场的影响
- 短期：直接打的是AI板块情绪。英伟达是这轮行情总龙头，财报附注被拿放大镜看，科技股风险偏好先收缩。传导到币市很直接：机构资金本来就是美股和加密一起配的，科技股一哆嗦，风险资产整体降仓，BTC买盘同步转谨慎。BTC现在$63,108横着，本身就在等方向，这种消息就是往天平上加砝码。
- 中期：如果后续更多AI公司被扒出类似表外承诺，市场会重估整条AI供应链，抛压不是一天两天的事。而BTC跟纳指的相关性一直摆在那，美股调整周期里币市很难独善其身，ETH $1,883这种低位晃的，弹性只会更大。

我的判断
说实话，我短期偏空。300亿美元的表外承诺本身不致命，致命的是它戳了“AI需求无限”这个叙事一刀——市场最怕的就是确定性松动。BTC在$63,100这个位置本来就在磨，纳指真因为这事儿回调，$63,000整数关口大概率要被测试，守不住下面空间就打开了。ETH更弱，$1,883已经在低位，联动下跌只会跌得更狠。想看多的人，至少等英伟达官方回应、这颗雷消化得差不多了再说，现在进去赌反弹，性价比不高。

Sometimes the most valuable part of a community has nothing to do with charts or price. content:
Yesterday was one of those days where even opening my wallet felt exhausting.

Bills were sitting on the table, work had gone badly, and I seriously thought about selling my crypto and disappearing from the whole community. What was the point?

That night, I joined a $DUSK  Network community voice chat mostly out of habit.

Nobody was talking about charts.

Then someone’s little kid suddenly grabbed the microphone and shouted, “Dad, the cat is in the sink!”

There was this weird silence.

Then everyone started laughing. The dad sounded completely defeated: “I’m sorry. This happens every day.”

For ten minutes, strangers talked about pets, terrible cooking, noisy neighbors, and kids refusing to sleep.

I barely spoke. I just listened.

It felt strangely comforting.

Dusk wasn’t important because of a token that night. It was simply where those random people happened to meet.

I didn’t sell.

Not because I expected anything from crypto.

I just remembered there were still real people behind the usernames.

What happened
Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott, together with the city council, filed the lawsuit. In addition to Kalshi and Polymarket, the defendants also include three major trading platforms: Coinbase, Robinhood, and Webull. Core allegation: these platforms provide local residents with sports event–related trading services without authorization. A key detail: the latter three are not the product providers; they only provide the entry points—yet they are still pulled into the case.

One-line translation: regulatory accountability is no longer aimed only at the platforms themselves; the channels that help them reach users are being held responsible too.

- Medium term: prediction markets are one of the core narratives of this latest crypto mainstream breakout. Even a compliance benchmark like Coinbase is named as a defendant. The industry will need to reassess the risk premise of “access equals risk.” A lawsuit doesn’t equal a conviction, but during the drawn-out standoff, valuations for the sector are likely to remain under pressure.
